---
title: Aerodrome ground access
author: Manuel Waltert
---

Aerodrome ground access describes how passengers, staff, cargo, and service vehicles reach the airport from the surrounding region. It includes roads, public transport, parking, rental-car facilities, curbside areas, and sometimes rail or metro stations integrated into the terminal.

## Access modes

Typical access modes include:

- private cars and parking;
- taxis, ride-hailing, and kiss-and-fly areas;
- buses and coaches;
- rail, metro, tram, or automated people movers;
- cycling and pedestrian access where relevant;
- service and cargo vehicle access.

## Operational role

Ground access affects passenger arrival patterns, terminal congestion, staff punctuality, curbside capacity, and resilience during disruptions. For airports close to urban areas, ground access can be a major capacity and environmental constraint.

## Data relevance

Relevant data include passenger mode share, road travel times, parking occupancy, curbside dwell time, public transport schedules, and disruption information.
